name: Strong-Projection Positivity under Adjacent Pair Completions
statement: Let $G\subseteq Q_F$ be nonempty and ample. Suppose three distinct missing tips $c,u,v$ give ample individual extensions with the same acquired three-coordinate support $I$, with $u=c^{\{i\}}$ and $v=c^{\{j\}}$. If both pair extensions $G\cup\{c,u\}$ and $G\cup\{c,v\}$ are dismantlable ample, then every nonempty strong reduction $G^D$, $\varnothing\ne D\subseteq F$, is dismantlable ample.
proof: Put $S=G\cup\{c\}$. The additions of $u$ and $v$ to $S$ acquire respectively $I\cup\{i\}$ and $I\cup\{j\}$. If some nonempty $G^D$ were nonpeelable, the strong-projection formula and rank-two extension invariance would make $S^D$ nonpeelable as well. Positivity of both repaired families would then force $D\subseteq(I\cup\{i\})\cap(I\cup\{j\})=I$ and $4-|D|\ge3$, so $D=\{k\}$ for some $k\in I$. In that reduction, the projected tips $c_k,u_k$ remain distinct adjacent ample additions with the same acquired two-coordinate support $I\setminus\{k\}$, and their pair extension is the reduction of the positive family $G\cup\{c,u\}$. Square-pair invariance forces $G^{\{k\}}$ to peel, a contradiction.
comments: The fixed verifier checks every coordinate subset in six controls and supplies twelve explicit one-coordinate overlap peelings of the certified 291-concept seed. This necessary projection condition does not by itself make the three-tip profile possible.
